guide.summary: The Hassan II Mosque, the city's two national museums, hotel dining rooms and Corniche tables, with breakfast cafés, bakeries and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
highlights: Villa Carl Ficke – Musée de la mémoire de Casablanca
Musée de la Photographie et des Arts Visuels de Casablanca
guide.tip: Plan around Tuesdays: Villa Carl Ficke and the Musée de la Photographie et des Arts Visuels both close that day, while Hassan II Mosque tours run every day, with no 11h tour on Friday.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Villa Carl Ficke and the Musée de la Photographie et des Arts Visuels both close on Tuesdays and otherwise open 10h to 18h. Hassan II Mosque tours run every day, with no 11h tour on Friday.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: The Hassan II Mosque charges foreign adults 140 dhs, residents 70 dhs and under-6s nothing, and its museum charges foreign adults 30 Dhs. Both national museums charge foreign visitors 50 DH and Moroccan adults 25 DH.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Rick's Café holds reserved tables for 15 minutes past your booking time and asks for 24 hours' notice to cancel. Royal Mansour Gourmet Boutique pastries must be ordered 24 hours ahead and collected at La Brasserie.

toolkit.label: Dress and rules
toolkit.copy: At the Hassan II Mosque, cover your shoulders, chest and knees; shorts are forbidden, shoes come off and bags can be left at the entrance. Rick's Café requires smart casual dress.

guide.dek: Book the first mosque tour of the day, keep Tuesday free of the two national museums, and reserve evening tables ahead.
intro: The Hassan II Mosque is seen on guided tours at fixed times. From Saturday to Thursday they start at 8h, 9h, 10h, 11h and 14h; on Friday there is no 11h tour. Foreign adults pay 140 dhs, residents and foreign students 70 dhs, and children under 6 go free. Cover your shoulders, chest and knees, since shorts are forbidden; you take your shoes off and can leave bags at the entrance. The mosque's museum, ticketed separately at 30 Dhs for foreign adults, opens from 9h to 16h.

Two museums run by the Fondation nationale des musées tell the city's own story. Villa Carl Ficke, the Musée de la mémoire de Casablanca at 119 Boulevard de la Résistance, holds temporary exhibitions and shows sculptures by Ikram Kabbaj outside. The Musée de la Photographie et des Arts Visuels on Rue Larache, in the old medina, opened on 23 June 2026 in a building designed by Tadao Ando, with an inaugural exhibition titled CASA. Both open from 10h to 18h and close on Tuesdays. Foreign visitors pay 50 DH and Moroccan adults 25 DH.

The Royal Mansour on Avenue des Forces Armées Royales gathers several tables under one roof. Le Rooftop, on the 23rd floor with views of the Hassan II Mosque, serves breakfast from 7am to 11am and a Sunday brunch from 1pm to 4pm at MAD 900, or MAD 450 for children under 12. La Grande Table Marocaine serves lunch and dinner daily, and La Brasserie serves an afternoon goûter from 3pm to 6pm. The hotel's Gourmet Boutique takes pastry orders 24 hours ahead for collection at La Brasserie.

Rick's Café at 248 Boulevard Sour Jdid serves lunch from 12:00 to 15:00 and dinner from 18:30 to 00:30, asks for smart casual dress and holds tables for 15 minutes. Its New Year's Eve evening on 31 December 2026 starts at 8pm and costs 1,500 MAD, with non-refundable tickets. On the Corniche, Le Cabestan by the El Hank lighthouse publishes a 2026 menu, and Morocco Mall in Ain Diab opens from 10h to 21h Sunday to Thursday and until 22h on Friday and Saturday. For a slower start, Bondi Coffee Kitchen in Gauthier serves breakfast all day, every day, from 9am.
summaryCards: Take a morning guided tour of the Hassan II Mosque, then see Villa Carl Ficke for the city's history on any day except Tuesday.
Start with breakfast at Bondi Coffee Kitchen in Gauthier from 9am, or at Le Pain Quotidien in Anfa from 07:30.
Villa Carl Ficke and the Musée de la Photographie close on Tuesdays, and Rick's Café holds reserved tables for only 15 minutes.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The Hassan II Mosque's paid-visits page, which carries a seasonal timetable, could not be read (redirect loop), so tour times come from the foundation's home page and may change with the season. The national museums' pages say both 'lundi au dimanche' and 'Fermé le mardi'; this guide follows the Tuesday closure. Hotel venues at the Sofitel Casablanca Tour Blanche, Le Doge and the Mövenpick, and Le Cabestan, Acajou and Le Jasmine, publish no opening hours; the Sofitel, Le Doge and Mövenpick venue pages carry no 2026 date. Bondi Coffee Kitchen's site shows no explicit 2026 date. Morocco Mall lists Aquadream and other attractions without hours or prices. Sites that could not be read: Villa des Arts (403), Four Seasons, Hyatt Regency and Radisson (403), Kenzi Tower (TLS error), % Arabica (418), PAUL Maroc (connection refused) and Musée Abderrahman Slaoui (domain did not resolve). Iloli publishes no address. No official sites were found for La Sqala, the Musée du Judaïsme Marocain, the Aïn Sebaâ zoo, Parc de la Ligue Arabe or several Corniche and city-centre restaurants, so the guide has no public park.
